I farm in Quzhou County with well irrigation, and I have been doing this for 35 years, so I will keep my plan practical and not too risky. My land is only 16.1 mu, my family has off-farm work, and I am already 68, so I will choose a simple arrangement that I can manage steadily. Cotton is my main crop and fits my usual system, so I will keep most of the land in cotton. I will still plant some stevia, but on a smaller area, because it needs careful management and I do not want to spread my labor too thin. I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed, because I want more stable emergence and yield, but I will avoid pushing inputs too high. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at key stages instead of irrigating too often. I will use enough fertilizer to secure yield, especially for cotton, but not waste money on excessive fertilizer. I will do rotary tillage because it is easier and lighter for me than deep ploughing, and it matches the labor I can organize at home. For pests, I will spray when needed in the normal number of rounds for these crops, because both cotton and stevia can lose yield quickly if I wait too long.
